title: Sep 29 Results + Sep 30 Preview: Three Wins and I'll Die on the Astros Hill
summary: 75% hit rate on Sep 29, but let's talk about that Astros loss—and why the Braves are it again.

content.value:
## Let Me Be Honest: We Crushed It (Mostly)

Look, I'm not here to sugarcoat anything. We went 3-1 yesterday and I'm supposed to do a victory lap? Please. That one loss—the Astros debacle—is eating at me more than the three wins are satisfying me. But that's what separates the drama critics from the cheerleaders: we don't celebrate mediocrity, even when it's technically success.

## The Good, The Bad, and The Astros

The Braves? **Hit.** The Yankees? **Hit.** The Padres? **Chef's kiss, hit.** But the Astros at a coin-flip 50% confidence? That's where we stumbled. And you know what? I'm not even mad about picking them. I'm mad we only had 50% confidence and still rolled with it. That's the kind of wishy-washy nonsense that makes me want to throw my keyboard through a window.

But here's the controversial take: **the model was right to be uncertain.** Sometimes the juice isn't worth the squeeze, and a 50% pick is basically the algorithm saying 'I have no idea, flip a coin.' We should've passed. We didn't. Lesson learned.

## Tomorrow's Move: Back to the Atlanta Well

So what's the play for September 30? We're going right back to the **Atlanta Braves**. Same matchup, same energy, same 61% confidence. Phillies at Braves, round two.

Cristopher Sánchez on the mound for Philly, Tyler Mahle for Atlanta. And here's my hot take that'll get me crucified: **Sánchez is overrated in big spots.** The guy's solid, sure, but Mahle at home with the Braves' lineup behind him? That's the recipe. Atlanta showed us yesterday they can handle this Phillies squad, and nothing changes overnight in baseball.

content.title: ⭐ Sep 30 Top Pick
content.sub: 61% win probability • Mahle vs Sánchez • Trust the home team again

content.value:
## The Blunt Truth About Running It Back

Some of you are thinking: 'Rico, why the same pick? Where's the creativity?' And to that I say: **this isn't creative writing class, it's winning.** The model likes the Braves again at the same number. The fundamentals haven't changed. The pitcher matchup still favors Atlanta. Why would we get cute just for the sake of variety?

If you're looking for hot takes, here's one: **betting against teams on back-to-back days just because 'they can't win both' is amateur hour.** That's gambler's fallacy dressed up as strategy. The Braves are the better team in this matchup today, and they'll be the better team tomorrow. It's that simple.

We ride with Atlanta. Again. And if it misses? I'll own it. But I'm not changing horses mid-stream because some people need their picks to be 'exciting.' Winning is exciting enough for me.

## Bottom Line

75% yesterday, one pick that haunts me, and tomorrow we're doubling down on what worked. The Braves delivered on Sep 29, and they'll deliver on Sep 30. Bet on it—or don't. But don't come crying when Atlanta cashes again and you were too scared to play the obvious.

**Rico out.** ✌️
